title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This sheet is not Grothendieck's own mathematics. The scan shows a typed page, upside down, headed 'n°357 – 56 –'. It is page 56 of Bourbaki rédaction (draft) no. 357. Grothendieck evidently reused it as scrap paper: his handwritten notes on L-functions, determinants of Frobenius and λ-structures are on the neighbouring sheets, and the handwritten '5' is the archive page number.

The typed text is part of the classical existence proof of Haar measure on a locally compact group G, using 'Haar covering numbers'. Notation:
- K is the space of continuous functions with compact support, and K_+ its non-negative part.
- For f, g in K_+ with g ≠ 0, (f:g) is the infimum of ||μ|| over positive discrete measures μ = Σ a_i ε_{s_i} with f ≤ γ(μ)g. Here γ(μ)g(x) = Σ a_i g(s_i^{-1}x), so (f:g) = inf Σ a_i over all such dominations.
- K_*^+(V) denotes the non-zero g in K_+ supported in V.

The page states and proves the following properties:
- (vi) 1/(f_0:f) ≤ (f:g)/(f_0:g) ≤ (f:f_0).
- (vii) Subadditivity: (f+f':g) ≤ (f:g)+(f':g).
- (viii) Approximate superadditivity. If h ≥ 1 on the support of f+f' and ε > 0, there is a compact neighbourhood V of e such that, for all g in K_*^+(V), (f+f':g) ≥ (f:g)+(f':g) − ε(h:g).

The proofs:
- (i)–(iii), stated on the previous typed page, are called obvious.
- (iv) is obvious since sup(γ(μ)g) ≤ ||μ|| sup g.
- (v), submultiplicativity (f:h) ≤ (f:g)(g:h), follows from ||μ*μ'|| = ||μ||·||μ'|| for positive measures. The text cites Chap. VII §1 n°1, i.e. Bourbaki Intégration ch. VII, or a direct computation. It also uses γ(μ)γ(μ') = γ(μ*μ').
- (vi) comes from applying (v) to the triples (f_0,f,g) and (f,f_0,g).
- For (viii), set F = f+f'+δh with δ > 0. The functions φ = f/F and φ' = f'/F, extended by 0 off supp(f+f'), lie in K and so are uniformly continuous. Choose V such that |φ(x)−φ(s)| ≤ η whenever s^{-1}x ∈ V. Then φ(x)g(s^{-1}x) ≤ (φ(s)+η)g(s^{-1}x) for g supported in V. Given a domination F ≤ Σ a_i g(s_i^{-1}x), and using f = φF, one gets f ≤ Σ a_i(φ(s_i)+η)g(s_i^{-1}·). The page stops here.
- The standard continuation: summing the corresponding bounds for f and f' gives (f:g)+(f':g) ≤ (1+2η)(F:g). Then (F:g) ≤ (f+f':g)+δ(h:g), and choosing δ and η small finishes the proof.

This is exactly the Weil/Cartan route to the existence of Haar measure as written up in Bourbaki, Intégration ch. VII §1. It has no relation to the L-function notes on the other side of the sheets.
errors: No mathematical errors. (vi) follows correctly from (v), since (f:g) ≤ (f:f_0)(f_0:g) and (f_0:g) ≤ (f_0:f)(f:g).
The claim f = φF holds because f vanishes off supp(f+f') and φ = f/F there.
The proof of (viii) is cut off at the page break, but the method is the standard one and is complete in principle.

ideas.what: Haar covering numbers (f:g), with submultiplicativity and approximate additivity, used to construct Haar measure
ideas.modern_name: Existence of Haar measure via Haar's covering-number (Weil–Cartan) method
ideas.usually_credited_to: A. Haar (1933), A. Weil (1940), H. Cartan (1940); expository form in Bourbaki, Intégration ch. VII (1963)
ideas.where_published: Bourbaki, Intégration, ch. VII §1 (this sheet is a Bourbaki draft, not a Grothendieck text)

ideas.what: ||μ*μ'|| = ||μ||·||μ'|| for positive (discrete) measures, used to get (f:h) ≤ (f:g)(g:h)
ideas.modern_name: Multiplicativity of total mass under convolution

missed.claim: Provenance and dating evidence: Grothendieck's L-function notes in cote 60 are written on the backs of a typed Bourbaki rédaction no. 357, page 56, on Haar measure. This document is probably connected with the preparation of Intégration ch. VII–VIII. It may help date this part of the notes to the 1960s Bourbaki period and documents his reuse of Bourbaki drafts. It is not a mathematical discovery.
missed.quote: n°357 - 56 - ... (par la vertu du Chap.VII, §1, n°1, ...)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Useful to archivists and historians for dating the manuscript and cross-referencing with the Bourbaki archives (archives-bourbaki.ahp-numerique.fr), which catalogue rédactions by number.

deep.surprise_reason: The typed verso is a standard Bourbaki draft of the classical Haar measure existence proof. It is unrelated to Grothendieck's L-function notes and contains nothing new; only its archival provenance is of mild interest.
transcription_corrections: The page image is upside down. It is a typed (typewriter) Bourbaki rédaction, not Grothendieck's handwriting. The handwritten '5' is the archive page number.
The machine transcription of the typed text is essentially correct. 'K_*^+(V)' denotes the non-zero functions in K_+ supported in V.
The page begins mid-list: properties (i)–(v) and the definition of (f:g) were on the previous typed page, 55, which is not in this sequence.
